rows.capability: Local identity, role grants and access workspace
rows.evidence: Entra signature/tenant/audience/scope validation; membership plus an explicit scoped RoleGrant is now required, with expiry, recorded revocation and firm/client/engagement scope enforced in the guard and reapplied inside each write transaction. Not implemented: session/access epoch revocation, segregation-of-duties combinations and a grant administration surface.

rows.capability: Client SharePoint site provisioning
rows.destinationOwner: Platform site-provisioning workers / site status UI
rows.evidence: Per-client repository bindings resolved per purpose (evidence/working), immutable provider-version identity recorded in DocumentVersion, and reads served from the version endpoint with eTag and SHA-256 verification; production fails closed without a binding. Not implemented: site provisioning, tenant consent, live permission verification and retention controls.

rows.capability: Quotation calculation and tender documents
rows.evidence: Pure fee model ported from the source: sum(hours × rate) → complexity → risk premium → discount with every stage rounded to two decimals half-to-even so the breakdown reconciles to the fee, plus input validation that fails closed and a canonical input hash. The configurable approval matrix is ported with its fail-safe Partner default. docs/migration/03-differential-report.md reports 46/46 checks matched. Not implemented: persisted quotation versions, tender/proposal documents, dispatch and client acceptance of an exact version.

rows.capability: Trial balance import and multi-period intake
rows.evidence: Bounded CSV upload to staging with sha256 duplicate detection, PG outbox, BullMQ parsing, transactional set-based mapping and zero-sum finalization. Monetary columns are numeric(28,6) with a six-decimal contract. A finalized import now publishes an immutable accepted balance version bound to that exact import version, with capability, state, completeness and zero-sum checks. Concurrent identical uploads now coalesce into one authoritative import, every stored object is tracked before its bytes exist, and a grace-period sweep removes only unreferenced objects while durable Graph evidence is reported for review. Not implemented: XLSX, multi-period/entity intake, sealed source acceptance and currency-aware publication.

rows.capability: Mapping memory and approved mappings
rows.destinationOwner: Fieldwork mapping workbench / reporting mapping approval
rows.evidence: Optimistic per-row versions, idempotency receipts and engagement-row locking, plus firm-scoped versioned taxonomies whose approved versions and lines are immutable by database trigger, and a mapping approval that binds one import's mapped rows to an exact taxonomy version by digest. Any later row change makes the approval stale, and publication now requires a current approval. Approved mappings now build client-scoped memory with the approval as provenance, and a read-only suggestion endpoint offers remembered codes (reporting unknown accounts, retired codes and already-mapped rows explicitly). Not implemented: allocation rules, statement layouts/financial packages, and the mapping UI.

rows.capability: Adjustment journals, plans and eligibility
rows.evidence: Client audit adjustment journals kept separate from the firm's own ledger: balanced double-entry drafts, posting under a distinct capability with a preparer/poster separation of duties, database-enforced balance and at-least-two-lines at posting, and a posted journal frozen except for one transition to REVERSED via a reversal journal that swaps the sides. Not implemented: adjustment plans, adjusted-balance snapshots, eligibility queries and the differences register.

rows.capability: Materiality and risk classification
rows.evidence: Pure calculator ported from the source with identical arithmetic: benchmark derivation from mapped sections with tax excluded from profit before tax, per-benchmark policy validation, PM/TE/SAD on a decimal-safe six-decimal primitive, risk bands with minimum owner rank, and an input hash. docs/migration/03-differential-report.md reports 14/14 checks matched against source-quoted fixtures. Assessments are now persisted against an exact published balance version and taxonomy version, require MATERIALITY_MANAGE to calculate and MATERIALITY_APPROVE to approve, forbid self-approval, become stale when a newer publication exists, and are frozen once approved. Risk is now persisted too: an append-only band-assessment series with the colour derived by the database from the recorded scores (a stored band that does not follow from its inputs is rejected), and mandatory Partner clearance (`RISK_PARTNER_CLEAR`) of the current red band. Risk owners are assigned against the current assessment with a minimum staffing rank enforced both in the service and by a database trigger, red bands require prior Partner clearance, and a user cannot assign a risk to themselves. The `START_FIELDWORK` lifecycle command now refuses to start from an unapproved or stale plan. Not implemented: routing risks into workprograms, the risk/planning UI, and the same staleness gate for later lifecycle steps.

rows.capability: Sampling runs, evidence and movements
rows.evidence: Deterministic engine ported from the source with the same fixed splitmix64 generator: MUS interval crossing, key-item threshold, seeded random draw, stratified key-item-plus-draw, zero-exposure exclusion, absolute-exposure selection with signed totals and a six-decimal coverage percentage. docs/migration/03-differential-report.md reports 33/33 checks matched overall. Not implemented: persisted immutable populations and execution records, physical evidence movements and procedure conclusions.

rows.capability: Review notes, reviews and completion
rows.evidence: Anchored review notes with grant-based authority: REVIEW_RAISE to raise, REVIEW_RESOLVE to resolve, the raiser can never resolve their own note, one OPEN→RESOLVED transition, and a resolved note is frozen by trigger while notes are never deleted; the database independently rejects a self-resolved or inconsistently shaped row. Not implemented: reviewer inbox, rework loop, revision-aware anchoring, SRM compilation and manager/Partner clearances.

rows.capability: Records archive, checkpoints and release evidence
rows.evidence: Transactionally ordered audit sidecars, canonical event format, SHA-256 predecessor chain, independent checkpoint manifest interface and scoped verifier. Concurrent writes, rollback and tampering are tested against PostgreSQL. No immutable archive bundle, live signed checkpoint storage, retention assurance or release checkpoint is implemented.

rows.capability: Firm billing, ledger and finance queries
rows.evidence: Firm-wide authorized chart, active/posting accounts, non-overlapping date-only periods, policy-gated balanced journal posting, immutable posted headers and lines, exact append-only reversing journals, trial balance query and Practice UI. PostgreSQL scope, balance, lock and race guards are implemented. Not implemented: invoices, payment allocations, credit notes, period reopening, bank reconciliation, monthly P/L and AR aging; full source parity remains incomplete.

rows.capability: Operations hosts, workers and scoped operations UI
rows.evidence: PostgreSQL outbox plus a reconciliation loop that republishes missing BullMQ jobs, with terminal-success handling and status fencing. Covers only the tb.import job family; no other operation types, no cancellation dispositions, no stale-worker fencing token.

rows.capability: API downloads, drafts, upload helpers and route guards
rows.evidence: Upload/mapping/finalize contracts validated by Zod at the HTTP boundary and an internal guard. No no-store download policy, draft handling or equivalent non-TB journeys.

rows.capability: Migrations, database checks, triggers and indexes
rows.destinationOwner: Prisma migrations plus reviewed PostgreSQL SQL
rows.evidence: Ten reviewed SQL migrations: append-only audit and lifecycle history, finalized-row and published-balance immutability, six-decimal monetary precision, compound firm/client/engagement scope foreign keys and grant scope/revocation/window check constraints. Check constraints, triggers, indexes and immutable-history coverage are still far short of the source's 252 tables.
